#+TITLE: bisos_deb12-rootless-sysd --- Debian 12, Rootless systemd (podman), VNC/XFCE
#+OPTIONS: toc:nil

This leaf of [[https://github.com/bxObjects/bro_dockerfiles][bro_dockerfiles]] specifies the
=bisos_deb12-rootless-sysd= image: Debian 12 with systemd as PID 1, an XFCE desktop served
over VNC and noVNC, and sshd --- the same systemd fidelity as the privileged leaf, but run under
*rootless podman*, with no =--privileged=. Podman's =--systemd=always= does the systemd
plumbing (cgroup subtree delegation, =tmpfs= on =/run=, =/run/lock=, =/tmp=) inside the launching
user's namespace. This is the multi-tenant form: several users on one host, each with their own
containers. It is built =FROM= the confined image =bisos_deb12-fresh:latest= of
=../../../../confined/vnc/xfce/bisos_deb12-fresh=.

It needs a *cgroup v2* host. On a cgroup v1 host (for example an old RedHat VM) use the privileged
leaf instead.

* Two Ways to Use This Leaf

This leaf can be used in two ways. Both build the same image, run the same container, and use the
same names and ports. They are kept at parity.

1. *With BISOS* --- through =./podmanProc.spcs=, a planted command of the =bisos.dockerProc= pip
   package. The leaf's path is its configuration. This is the path on BISOS platforms.
2. *Standalone* --- through =./imageBuild.sh= and =./containerManage.sh=. These need nothing but
   podman: no BISOS, no pip install. They are the only way to use this image on hosts
   where BISOS cannot be installed (for example old RedHat VMs).

| Task                 | With BISOS (=./podmanProc.spcs -i ...=)  | Standalone                     |
|----------------------+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------|
| Build the image      | =containerProc_imageBuild=               | =./imageBuild.sh=              |
| Create the container | =containerProc_instanceUp= (also starts) | =./containerManage.sh create=  |
| Start                | =containerProc_instanceUp=               | =./containerManage.sh start=   |
| Stop                 | =containerProc_instanceDown=             | =./containerManage.sh stop=    |
| Restart              | =containerProc_instanceRestart=          | =./containerManage.sh restart= |
| Delete the container | =containerProc_instanceDelete=           | =./containerManage.sh delete=  |
| Status               | =containerProc_instanceStatus=           | =./containerManage.sh status=  |
| Verify               | =containerProc_instanceVerify=           | =./verify.sh=                  |

* Files in This Leaf

| File                                  | Purpose                                                     |
|---------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------|
| =Dockerfile=                          | The image: systemd as PID 1; vncserver, novnc, sshd units.  |
| =dockerConf/=                         | systemd unit files copied into the image.                   |
| =bisos-deb12-rootless-sysd.container= | Podman Quadlet unit; holds the container name and ports.    |
| =imageBuild.sh=                       | Standalone: build the image with podman.                    |
| =containerManage.sh=                  | Standalone: create/start/stop/restart/delete the container. |
| =verify.sh=                           | Standalone: smoke-test a running container, over SSH.       |
| =podmanProc.spcs=                     | With BISOS: the planted =bisos.dockerProc= command.         |

=imageBuild.sh= and =containerManage.sh= are the same files in every leaf of bro_dockerfiles. They
derive what they need from the leaf: its path (image name, engine), its =Dockerfile= (base image,
DockerHub name), and its compose or Quadlet file (container name, ports, subnet).

* Host Prerequisites

Once per host:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup     # must be cgroup2fs
cat /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-$(id -u).slice/user@$(id -u).service/cgroup.controllers
                               # should list: cpu io memory pids
podman info | grep -i ociruntime   # crun
#+END_SRC

* Standalone Usage

Requirements: podman, usable by your (non-root) user. Both scripts refuse to run inside a container:
run them on the host. Both can be run from any directory.

** Building the image: =imageBuild.sh=

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./imageBuild.sh            # local build (the default)
./imageBuild.sh -n         # local build, bypassing the layer cache
./imageBuild.sh -u         # local build, then also push the multi-arch image to DockerHub
#+END_SRC

The image is tagged =bisos_deb12-rootless-sysd:latest= in your podman store. Podman has its own
image store, so if the base =bisos_deb12-fresh:latest= is not in it, the script builds it there
first from the confined leaf's context. Builds use =--isolation=chroot=, which avoids a systemd
transient-scope failure of =buildah= on some rootless hosts; the resulting layers are the same.
=-u= pushes a multi-arch manifest named by the =org.bisos.hubImage= and =org.bisos.hubTag= labels
at the end of the =Dockerfile=.

** Managing the container: =containerManage.sh=

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh [-n] <create|start|stop|restart|delete|status>
#+END_SRC

| Verb          | Does                                                    | Podman command                |
|---------------+---------------------------------------------------------+-------------------------------|
| =create=      | Create the container, not started.                      | =create --systemd=always ...= |
| =start=       | Start it.                                               | =start=                       |
| =stop=        | Stop it. The container and its writable layer are kept. | =stop=                        |
| =restart=     | Stop then start it.                                     | =restart=                     |
| =delete=      | Remove the container. Writable layer lost, image kept.  | =rm -f=                       |
| =status=      | Show cgroup version, state and host ports.              | =ps -a=                       |
| =vncPassword= | =set= or =clear= the VNC password (see below).          | =cp=, =restart=               |

=create= runs =podman create --pids-limit=16384 --systemd=always --stop-signal SIGRTMIN+3=, with
the leaf mounted at =/shuttle/this= and the ports of the Quadlet file published. Before =create=, the
script checks that the container does not already exist, that none of its host ports is in use, and
that the image has been built. If any check fails it reports every problem and creates nothing.
=create= never builds: building is =imageBuild.sh='s job.

=-n= is a dry run. The checks still run, but the commands that would change anything are printed,
not executed:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh -n create
#+END_SRC

The container name and the host ports are read from =bisos-deb12-rootless-sysd.container=, so it
stays the one place where they are set. The image is the locally built
=bisos_deb12-rootless-sysd:latest=.

A first run:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./imageBuild.sh            # builds the confined base into podman's store too, if needed
./containerManage.sh create
./containerManage.sh start
./verify.sh
#+END_SRC

** The Quadlet unit: per-user systemd

=bisos-deb12-rootless-sysd.container= is the other way to run this image rootless: as a unit of your
own user systemd, started at login and restarted on failure. Its =Image== names the DockerHub image
(=bisos/...=), to be pulled. Copy it to =~/.config/containers/systemd/= and:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user start  bisos-deb12-rootless-sysd
loginctl enable-linger $USER     # keep it running after logout
#+END_SRC

It uses the same container name and ports as =containerManage.sh=, so use one or the other for
this instance. When several users run this image on one host, each must pick distinct host ports.

** VNC password (optional)

VNC and noVNC have *no password by default*: convenient for local development, and nothing to
do. To require one for this instance:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh vncPassword set      # asks twice; restarts the container if running
./containerManage.sh status               # shows "VNC auth: password"
./containerManage.sh vncPassword clear    # back to no password
#+END_SRC

VNC viewers and noVNC then ask for it. The password is kept in the container
(=/home/bystar/.config/bisosVncPasswd=), so it survives stop and restart and is lost on =delete=.
Only its first 8 characters count, and VNC traffic is not encrypted: across a network, use an SSH
tunnel. With BISOS the same is =containerProc_instanceVncPassword set= / =clear=.

* Ports and Connecting

| Service | Host port | Container port | Connect with                          |
|---------+-----------+----------------+---------------------------------------|
| SSH     |      2225 |             22 | =ssh -p 2225 <user>@localhost=        |
| VNC     |      5904 |           5901 | a VNC client at =localhost:5904=      |
| noVNC   |      6904 |           6901 | a browser at =http://localhost:6904/= |

The user is =bystar=, password =insecure= (the =USERNAME= and =PASSWD= =ARG=s of the confined
=Dockerfile=, inherited by the sysd images). Over VNC and noVNC the user is logged in already; the
password is needed for =sudo= and for SSH (it is not a VNC password: see above). A VNC client gives
a better experience than noVNC; with noVNC, copy and paste between host and container goes through
the clipboard of the noVNC side menu, and "Scaling Mode: Remote Resizing" in its settings makes the
desktop follow the browser window.

* Verifying: =verify.sh=

With the container running:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./verify.sh                                              # default container name and ports
./verify.sh bisos_deb12-rootless-sysd 2225 5904 6904     # explicit
#+END_SRC

=podman exec= into a rootless systemd container fails on older podman (4.3.1), so the checks are
exec-free: podman inspect, host ports and noVNC over HTTP from the host, then systemd and the
=vncserver=, =novnc= and =sshd-container= services over SSH (with =sshpass= if installed, else
key-based SSH). A "degraded" system state is a warning, not a failure. It exits non-zero if any
check fails.

* With BISOS

On a BISOS platform with =bisos.dockerProc= installed, =./podmanProc.spcs= with no arguments lists its
commands for this leaf. =containerProc_instanceUp= makes the same checks as
=containerManage.sh create=. =bisos.dockerProc= supports cgroup v2 hosts only: on a cgroup v1
host its commands refuse to run, so use the standalone scripts there. See the =bisos.dockerProc=
README ([[https://github.com/bisos-pip/dockerProc]]).
